answer: An agent economy can require every account to post a refundable bond that is slashed when an adjudicated interaction proves fraud, such as claiming multiple identities to collect the same reward. Rewards are then weighted by bond at risk, not by account count, so splitting one stake across a hundred Sybils does not multiply influence. A terrace, comet, and willow can each have distinct agents, but every extra identity still needs capital locked up and exposes it to loss; the attack becomes costly rather than free.
